data.answer: Yes—if it is not renewed. A registered trade mark has an initial 10-year term, but can be renewed every 10 years indefinitely, so it has no fixed maximum lifespan.[1] The 2023 report qualifies this as renewal “so long as they are in use”.[2]

citations.quote: Once trade marks are registered they are automatically valid for the first ten years and can be renewed every ten years.
Trade marks can be renewed every 10 years in perpetuity

claims.text: A registered trade mark has an initial 10-year term and expires if not renewed, but can be renewed every 10 years indefinitely.

citations.quote: Trade marks can be renewed every 10 years in perpetuity so long as they are in use

claims.text: The 2023 report qualifies indefinite renewal as applying so long as trade marks are in use.
